title: Fernão do Pó sights Bioko
description: The Portuguese navigator charts the island that bears his name for the next five centuries, finding Bubi people already farming it.

title: Spain acquires Fernando Pó
description: By the Treaty of El Pardo, Portugal cedes Fernando Pó and Annobón and a claim on the Guinea coast to Spain, which wants bases for the Río de la Plata slave trade.

title: British found Port Clarence
description: Leasing the island from Spain, Britain builds a base against the slave trade, the town known today as Malabo.

title: Spain resumes control
description: Spain tells Britain it will take the island back and rebuilds its own colony, the town being renamed Santa Isabel.

title: Berlin Conference recognises Spanish claims
description: The European powers confirm Spanish rights to a mainland territory around the Muni estuary, much smaller than Madrid hoped.

title: Treaty of Paris fixes the mainland borders
description: France and Spain cut Río Muni down to 26,000 square kilometres, leaving Spain with the small enclave the mainland province remains.

title: Territory split by the Spanish Civil War
description: Río Muni's garrison joins Franco's rising while Fernando Pó holds out for the Republic until the nationalists take it.

title: Spanish Guinea becomes two Spanish provinces
description: Colonial status ends as Río Muni and Fernando Pó are made overseas provinces of metropolitan Spain.

title: Autonomy granted
description: After a referendum the two provinces gain a common autonomous government, the last step before independence.

title: Independence from Spain
description: Equatorial Guinea becomes independent with Francisco Macías Nguema as its first president.

title: Macías begins his reign of terror
description: A failed coup within months of independence sends the president into mass arrests and executions that over a decade drive a third of the people into exile.

title: President for life
description: Macías Nguema proclaims himself president for life and rules through his family militia while the economy collapses.

title: Obiang overthrows Macías
description: The president's nephew Teodoro Obiang seizes power; Macías is tried and executed by Moroccan guards.

title: Oil discovered
description: Large offshore reserves turn the country into one of sub-Saharan Africa's biggest oil producers, enriching the ruling family while most stay poor.

title: Mercenary coup attempt foiled
description: Zimbabwe seizes a plane of mercenaries en route to overthrow Obiang for the oil interests behind them; financiers including Mark Thatcher are later convicted.

title: Obiang chairs the African Union
description: President Teodoro Obiang took over the rotating chairmanship of the African Union for a year.

title: Vice-president convicted in France
description: A French court found the president's son, Vice-President Teodorín Obiang, guilty of money laundering, seizing his Paris mansion and luxury cars and giving him a suspended sentence.

title: Foreign mercenaries intercepted at Ebibeyin
description: Security forces intercepted foreign mercenaries at Ebibeyin on the Cameroon border in what the government called a coup attempt, and a crackdown on the opposition followed.

title: Seat on the UN Security Council
description: Equatorial Guinea sat on the UN Security Council for the first time.

title: Bata explosions
description: Explosions at a military barracks kill about a hundred people.
